Lessons.Title: Types of Angles
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will classify angles as acute, obtuse, and straight, and to identify and draw acute and obtuse angles.
In previous lessons, you learned to measure angles and draw angles of given measurements. You saw that a \(90^\circ\) angle is called a right angle and is formed by two perpendicular lines. You are also familiar with some benchmark angle measurements.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Fractions of 120 and 360 (10 minutes); Activity 1: Sorting Angles (10 minutes); Activity 2: What is It, Really? (10 minutes); Activity 3: Small Angles, Large Angles (15 minutes); Cool-down: Obtuse, Acute, and Straight Angles (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Acute angles measure less than 90°; right angles equal 90°; obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°; straight angles equal 180°.

Edulytics authored guidance: Measure or estimate the actual angle opening before classifying. Separate acute, right, obtuse, and straight by degree boundaries. A 130° angle is obtuse and a 45° angle is acute regardless of segment lengths.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Classify angles of 45°, 130°, and 180°.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
